items.title: Longer family leave takes effect November 26
items.body: Birth leave rises to 20 weeks, or 34 for single-parent families, from November 26 under a Royal Decree-law. Bereavement leave rises to 10 working days. Congress's standing committee must still validate it. PP secretary general Miguel Tellado called the new rights "papel mojado" (worthless).

items.title: Cabinet approves minimum-wage tax withholding cut for 2027
items.body: The cabinet approved Royal Decree-law 38/2026, pending Congress validation. From January 1, 2027, it would end IRPF (personal income tax) withholding for SMI (minimum wage) earners and cut it for pay below €23,171.89 a year. The SMI would rise 5.3% to €18,004 gross a year. Workers would no longer wait for a refund.

items.title: Euribor rises above 3.3% as mortgages climb
items.body: November's Euribor average is above 3.3% as markets expect a December ECB rate rise to 2.75%. An annual review of a €150,000 mortgage over 25 years with a one-point spread would add about €90 a month. Higher energy prices from the Middle East war have pushed eurozone CPI inflation to 4%.

items.title: Election model favours PP–Vox majority on November 29
items.body: El País's model gives PP and Vox an 83% chance of a majority in the November 29 election after allowing for a leftward polling trend. Its central estimate gives them about 190 seats; 176 are needed. The PSOE has narrowed the PP's polling lead to just over two points. These are simulations, not election results.

items.title: Canary Islands declare emergency over sea arrivals
items.body: The Canary Islands declared a level 2 emergency on November 25 after more than 3,000 migrants arrived by sea in three days. The military emergency unit (UME) travels to El Hierro on November 26 to provide triage and primary care. Regional authorities say healthcare and child-care capacity is overstretched.

items.title: Annual VAT filing plan draws cash-flow warnings
items.body: The cabinet approved an annual VAT return option on November 24 for autónomos (self-employed) billing under €85,000. Those opting in would still make advances in April, July, and October and lose the right to defer or split payments. Trade groups warn that advances based on the previous year's quota could strain struggling businesses.

items.title: Grosso Napoletano wins world pizza chain title
items.body: Madrid-founded Grosso Napoletano topped the 50 Top World Artisan Pizza Chains 2026 ranking for the third time, after wins in 2023 and 2024. It has 45 venues across Spain. Five other Spanish chains made the top 50, so six Spanish chains are on the list.

items.title: Draft report flags high-speed rail detection gaps
items.body: A draft rail accident report says public rail company Adif approved a system in 2020 despite knowing it could not detect rail breaks. Investigators urge urgent safety measures on the Madrid–Andalucía high-speed line after the Adamuz crash killed 46. They say the rail broke 22 hours before the crash.

items.title: Rental data dispute accompanies Madrid decree challenge
items.body: The Housing Ministry says Tax Agency data show about 475,000 more rental homes in 2021–2025, despite fewer ads. Madrid's government will appeal the housing decree validated November 12 as unconstitutional. It extends by two years contracts expiring before the end of 2028 and suspends evictions of vulnerable tenants without alternative housing.

items.title: Mortgage signings rise while home sales fall
items.body: September home mortgage signings rose 2.3% to 46,469, while sales fell 13.4%, according to INE (national statistics institute). The average loan reached €178,352, and the average interest rate rose to 3.05%. January–September signings reached 383,366, the highest total for that period since 2010.
